Task: Develop a complete lesson plan for teaching probability to high-school students.

Lesson Plan: Introduction to Probability (High-School Level)  
Duration: 75 minutes (1 class period)  
Grade Level: 9–10 (adaptable for 11–12)

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Big Idea / Essential Question
────────────────────────────────────────
• How can we quantify uncertainty and use probability to predict the likelihood of events?  
• Where do we encounter probability in everyday life and in future STEM fields?

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Learning Objectives (Student-Friendly “I Can” Statements)
────────────────────────────────────────
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to …
1. Define probability as a ratio comparing favorable outcomes to total possible outcomes.  
2. Distinguish between theoretical and experimental probability.  
3. Calculate probabilities of single events (simple probability) and complementary events.  
4. Use probability models (tables, tree diagrams) to organize outcomes.  
5. Communicate reasoning using correct probability notation (P(A)).  

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Standards Alignment (sample – adapt to your state)
────────────────────────────────────────
CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS.CP.A.1 – Understand and apply basic concepts of probability.  
CCSS.MATH.PRACTICE.MP4 – Model with mathematics.  
NGSS Science & Engineering Practice: Analyzing and interpreting data.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Materials & Technology
────────────────────────────────────────
• Individual student kits: 2 six-sided dice, 1 coin, 20 colored beads (10 red, 10 blue) in opaque bag.  
• Whiteboard or digital display; markers.  
• Student handouts: Guided notes + practice sheet.  
• Exit-ticket slips / online form (if digital).  
• Optional: Desmos “Marbleslides Probability” or GeoGebra simulation, document camera for live demos.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. Vocabulary
────────────────────────────────────────
Event, outcome, sample space, probability (P), theoretical, experimental, complementary events, fair, equally likely.

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Lesson Sequence
────────────────────────────────────────
A. Hook / Engagement (5 min)  
   – Display two headlines: “Rain chance today: 40%” and “NBA player hits 85% of free throws.”  
   – Quick think-pair-share: What does each percentage mean? Are they guarantees?  
   – Transition: “These numbers come from probability—today we’ll figure out how they are calculated.”

B. Direct Instruction & Modeling (15 min)  
   1. Definition and formula: P(A) = (# favorable outcomes) / (total outcomes).  
   2. Visual: Tree diagram of flipping a coin (H/T).  
   3. Theoretical vs. experimental probability: Use dice example; highlight long-run frequencies.  
   4. Complementary events: P(A) + P(not A) = 1.

C. Guided Practice: Station Rotation (20 min)  
   Station 1 – Coin Flips (experimental): Each pair flips a coin 20 times; record heads count; compare to theoretical 0.5.  
   Station 2 – Dice Sums (theoretical): Use table to list sums 2–12; calculate probability of getting a 7.  
   Station 3 – Mystery Bag (beads): Without looking, draw one bead, record color, replace. Compute experimental probability of red; compare across class with teacher’s revealed theoretical ratio.  
   Teacher circulates, prompts students to articulate reasoning and check calculations.

D. Whole-Class Synthesis (10 min)  
   – Collect data on board from each group’s experiments. Discuss why results differ from theory but tend toward it with larger trials (Law of Large Numbers conceptually).  
   – Emphasize notation and complement: If P(red) = 0.5, what is P(blue)?

E. Independent Practice (15 min)  
   Handout problems:  
   1. A fair spinner has 8 equal sections (3 red, 5 blue). Find P(red), P(not red).  
   2. Draw tree diagram for coin + die (outcomes 12). Probability of tails and rolling 6?  
   3. Challenge: Two-step scenario—drawing a card (without replacement) then flipping coin.  
   Teacher provides immediate feedback / conferencing.

F. Closure (5 min)  
   Exit Ticket (2 questions):  
   1. Explain the difference between theoretical and experimental probability in one sentence.  
   2. A bag has 4 green, 6 yellow marbles. What’s P(green)? Show fraction, decimal, percent.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Assessment
────────────────────────────────────────
Formative: Observation at stations, questioning, guided practice responses.  
Summative: Exit ticket (today) + homework set; quiz at end of short unit.

Rubric sample (Exit Ticket Q2):  
– Correct fraction 4/10 (1)  
– Simplified 2/5 (0.5)  
– Decimal 0.4 (0.5)  
– Percent 40% (0.5)  
Total 2.5 pts.

────────────────────────────────────────
8. Differentiation / UDL
────────────────────────────────────────
• Visual supports: color-coded tree diagrams, manipulatives.  
• Auditory: Verbal explanations; peer discussion.  
• Kinesthetic: Physical coin flips, bead draws.  
• Extension for advanced learners: Introduce independent vs. dependent events, or calculate probability of getting at least one head in three flips.  
• Support for struggling learners: Provide sentence starters (“P(A) equals …”), anchor charts, small-group reteach during Independent Practice.  
• ELL scaffolds: Vocabulary cards with icons; allow responses in native language + glossary.  
• Accessibility: Large-print handouts, provide digital simulations for students unable to manipulate physical objects.

────────────────────────────────────────
9. Homework / Extension
────────────────────────────────────────
A. Flipped extension video: “Why 50/50 Doesn’t Always Mean 50/50” (3-min clip) + reflection question.  
B. Practice worksheet: 10 mixed problems (simple, complementary, experimental vs. theoretical).  
C. Real-world application: Track local weather forecast probability for 5 days; record actual outcome; compute experimental probability of rain; write one-paragraph reflection.

────────────────────────────────────────
10. Reflection (Teacher Notes, post-lesson)
────────────────────────────────────────
• What proportion of students met the objectives?  
• Which station generated the most misconceptions?  
• How will results inform the next lesson on compound events and conditional probability?

────────────────────────────────────────
11. Resources / References
────────────────────────────────────────
• Boaler, J. (2019). Limitless Mind – Chapter on Mistakes & Risk.  
• NCTM Illuminations: “Adjustable Spinner” interactive.  
• Desmos Classroom Activity: “Lucky Numbers.”  
• Khan Academy Probability Basics (for homework or intervention videos).

────────────────────────────────────────
End of Lesson Plan
